assessments.reasoning: Open Data Commons identifies its English full legal text at /licenses/pddl/1-0/ as Public Domain Dedication and License (PDDL) v1.0. Its reported digest 09ecade0250eba538cc68145b8f5448eb44cf8340a414665f7f5c12872102faa matches the claim. The preamble, definition of Document, §2.1 and §§3.1–3.3 agree on the sequence.

The Index scope includes relevant data and public-domain dedications. Its Related legal instrument row includes a distinct dedication with a documented connection to licensing. PDDL supplies that connection within the same instrument through its backup grant. The table supports the proposed mapping without naming PDDL individually.

limitations: The Index criteria do not prescribe an exclusive classification for every hybrid instrument. Section 3.3 is a genuine license and the related-instrument mapping describes the dedication as a whole. Active is the intended lifecycle value. Current admission is unverified.

The defined Work can be the database, its data, or both as offered by the rightsholder. Third-party contents require their own authority. Section 2 excludes database-making or operating programs, patents and trademarks. Section 3.4 recognizes jurisdictional limits for moral rights. No particular dedication, redistribution right or installation eligibility follows from the page.
reasoning: The PDDL v1.0 preamble describes a public-domain objective and explains why the instrument provides alternatives across jurisdictions. Section 2.1 expressly identifies both the dedication and the fallback license. Section 3.1 dedicates the Work and relinquishes copyright and database rights. Section 3.2 waives rights and claims if dedication is inapplicable. Section 3.3 grants a worldwide, royalty-free, non-exclusive license if both earlier mechanisms are inapplicable. The Index expressly includes distinct dedications as related legal instruments. This mapping preserves the whole instrument and the conditional force of §3.3, as SCES §3 requires.
